The Cobb County Police Department said it was investigating the fatality at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24km) from Atlanta, according to the BBC's news partner CBS. Police did not specify what ride was involved, but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, with riders being helped off by workers. Six Flags Over Georgia said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones." Officials have not said how the person was killed. The BBC has contacted local police and fire authorities, as well as park officials. Witnesses told local media they saw a man ejected from the ride, accounts that the BBC has not verified. Local outlet 11Alive quoted a witness saying the man fell from the rollercoaster on to the roof of a haunted house attraction. A park spokesperson said in a statement that its team and local authorities had responded immediately, and they were co-operating on an investigation into the incident. Mableton Mayor Michael Owens said the city's public safety director was co-ordinating with local police and park security on the situation. The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five. Six Flags is the largest amusement park operator in North America, with 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico. The incident comes just weeks after one of its parks in southern California announced it would close the popular X2 roller coaster after more than 100 people alleged brain injuries from the ride. In its twice-yearly World Economic Outlook, the IMF said global growth had withstood the Middle East conflict better than feared over the past six months. It said the rerouting of oil supplies away from the strait of Hormuz, and the release of strategic energy stocks, had helped to contain the impact on oil prices from the US-Iran war. However, it warned that emergency stocks are now depleted, and high debt levels and deficits in many countries could leave governments with little capacity to protect consumers from any future jump in prices. “Without shoring up supply capacity and replenishing policy buffers, the global economy could soon test the limits of resilience,” it said. “Inventories in energy markets are dwindling and additional geopolitical shocks could still transmit rapidly through prices and supply disruptions.” The International Energy Agency announced the largest-ever emergency releases of oil stocks on to the market in March this year, and promised to accelerate it after a meeting of oil ministers last month . But in a sign of the system’s vulnerability, the US strategic petroleum reserve was recently reported to have fallen to its lowest level since 1982. Last week, Donald Trump agreed a deal with Vladimir Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on US imports of Russian diesel in an attempt to bring down prices at the pumps, which analysts said would have little “meaningful” effect. The World Economic Report was published on Tuesday in Bangkok, where the IMF and World Bank are holding their annual meetings this week, with finance ministers and central bankers scheduled to attend. clusters.text: Protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Electoral Officer Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise, at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on Monday. | Photo Credit: SUDHAKARA JAIN Protesters who tried to march to the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka’s office in Bengaluru on Monday, to condemn the Delhi Police’s treatment of demonstrators protesting against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), faced similar heavy-handedness from the Bengaluru City Police, with at least 100 people detained, and students, lawyers, and women protesters allegedly manhandled. Senior journalist and activist Aakar Patel was also detained. The police threatened journalists covering the protest and ordered them to leave the spot, while three photographers were manhandled, despite repeatedly identifying themselves as members of the Press. Several protesters, most of them students, were forcibly pushed into buses by police personnel, many of whom were not in uniform. Male police personnel were seen forcing women protesters into buses, with the police arguing that the protesters would return to the spot if they were released. A senior police officer, however, defended the actions, arguing that the police did not know about the protest and were taken by surprise. Given only Freedom Park is the designated protest site, they were bound to detain protesters outside that venue. He also admitted that since the police were not aware, the force included mostly male personnel. The protest was organised by Left student and youth organisations across Karnataka, which planned marches to the CEO’s office in Bengaluru and Deputy Commissioners’ offices in other districts. They demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of SIR of electoral rolls. In Bengaluru, the protesters assembled near K.R. He raised his price target to $285 from $160, about 24% above Friday's close of $229.13. Going straight from BofA's lowest rating to its highest is rare. Liani didn't just adjust his numbers. Alcaraz still had a mathematical chance of stopping Zverev until he was beaten 7-5 7-6 (7-4) by Belgium's Zizou Bergs in the third round on Monday. "It's been a fantastic season for me. clusters.title: Southwest monsoon withdraws from Jharkhand, IMD reports normal rainfall
also: Monsoon withdraws from Jharkhand with 2 pc rainfall deficit
clusters.text: Ranchi: The southwest monsoon completely withdrew from Jharkhand on Monday, raising hopes of favourable weather for Durga Puja and Navaratri celebrations across the state, Ranchi office of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) officials said.The head of the Ranchi office of the IMD, Baburaj PP, said, “The withdrawal process began on Oct 3, two days ahead of the normal date of Oct 5, and covered the rest of the state on Monday.”The monsoon had earlier withdrawn from Garhwa, Chatra, Palamu, Latehar, and Lohardaga, besides parts of Gumla, Ranchi, Hazaribag, and Koderma. On Monday, the withdrawal covered the remaining areas of Gumla, Ranchi, Hazaribag, and Koderma, Simdega, West Singhbhum, East Singhbhum, Seraikela-Kharsawan, Khunti, Ramgarh, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Giridih, Jamtara, Deoghar, Dumka, Pakur, Godda, and Sahibganj, he added.“The southwest monsoon had entered Jharkhand on June 12 and covered the entire state by June 30. Both its onset and withdrawal were broadly in line with normal patterns,” he said.Jharkhand recorded 1,005.7 mm of cumulative seasonal rainfall against the long-period average of 1,022.9 mm, a deficit of just 2%, which falls within the IMD’s normal rainfall category, the Met office said.The IMD has forecast morning fog or mist and partly cloudy skies over the next few days. Baharagora recorded 36.8°C, the state’s highest maximum temperature, while Latehar reported 16°C, the lowest minimum temperature during the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Monday.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
